newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Karrie ends debut below issue price.
newsitem.headline: HK's Karrie ends debut below issue price.

text.p: Shares of computer casing manufacturer Karrie International Holdings Ltd ended their trading debut at a low of HK$1.02 on Monday, down HK$0.13 or 11.3 percent from the issue price of HK$1.15 per share.
Analysts said investors were taking profit as soon as the shares began trading in the morning.
"Investors started to dump the stock when they saw Karrie's share price dropping soon after trading began," said Ben Kwong, director of research of Dharmala Securities.
Karrie shares hit a high of HK$1.40 per share. A total of 36.36 million shares worth HK$42.29 million changed hands.
Analysts said the company's core business activity did not have a niche market and investors felt earnings prospects were not bright.
"The company's fundamentals is not so attractive," said Kwong. "The product that they make, computer casing, is not a unique thing."
Karrie was in the low-tech computer industry with a low profit margin, said Seapower Securities senior research manager Sunny Chan.
Karrie offered 90 million new shares in the initial public offering (IPO) in Hong Kong. The IPO was 60.7 times subscribed.
